paper.central_claim: Polaris, a Godel-agent framework for small language models, turns failures into small persistent policy-code patches through reflection, experience abstraction (compact reusable strategies) and minimal patch repair with conservative execution checks; with a 7B model it yields consistent gains over the base policy and competitive baselines (CoT-SC) on MGSM, DROP, GPQA and LitBench, showing recursive self-improvement is viable with SLMs.
paper.title: Polaris: A Gödel Agent Framework for Small Language Models through Experience-Abstracted Policy Repair

gap.author_gap: Godel-agent recursive self-improvement is tied to frontier-scale LLMs; at 7B the framework's growing context causes OOM and tool-call errors, so it is unclear whether compact models can sustain recursive policy repair.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete, evidenced failure of the nearest framework under stated constraints (Table 1), but the residue is a resource and engineering limit of one framework configuration, not a demonstration that other small-model-friendly optimizers or memory-light loops fail.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Godel Agent (Yin et al. 2024) directly extended; Darwin Godel Machine contrasted textually; Reflexion/Self-Refine/CRITIC are response-level; prompt/program optimizers and skill/memory systems are not discussed as neighbors.
gap.residue: Rollback, regression checks, and stability still absent; success in only 43-45% of runs at 7B.
gap.stakes: Local deployment of self-improving agents with small models.
gap.method_response: Limit retained reflections, abstract them into strategies, patch minimally, and cap memory.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether abstraction (versus simply smaller context) causes the gains; guardrails; compute-matched comparison.
unresolved: Contribution of experience abstraction versus reduced memory/sample count

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A fixed reflection-abstraction-patch loop lets a Qwen2.5-7B policy reach higher test accuracy than its base policy in about 43-45% of 10-hour runs (best-so-far, success labelled on test), and a reduced-memory Godel Agent baseline almost never completes; neither the share of runs with net gain nor the contribution of abstraction is isolated.

assessment.note: Author-reported only; nothing was run by us. The claim of 'consistent gains' is retained as stated but is not supported at that strength.

G.reason: Evidenced bottleneck (Godel Agent context growth at 7B) with a clear baseline, but residue is a resource limit of one framework, and other small-model self-improvement/optimizer neighbors are not compared.

M.reason: Reflection to abstraction to minimal patch is a coherent mechanism for context control, but why abstraction rather than a smaller context drives gains is untested and the improver is a fixed prompt pipeline.

X.reason: Algorithms, prompts and run categories are given and the failure boundary is candid, but acceptance is execution-only, rollback is intentionally omitted, and conflict or staleness handling is absent.

E.measurement.reason: Benchmark accuracy/F1 are credible validators and bootstrap CIs are mentioned for two datasets, but test sets are small (100-250), the summary metric is a maximum relative improvement over successful runs, and success is defined by test gain.

E.causality.reason: Baselines are the base policy and CoT-SC; the Godel Agent baseline fails to run, there is no ablation of experience abstraction or memory reduction, and evolved policies add inference calls that CoT-SC does not match.

E.holdout.reason: Validation failures feed reflection and a separate test set exists, but runs are labelled successful by test improvement and best-so-far trajectories are reported with no disjoint promotion or selection split.

E.statistics.reason: Ten runs per cell with failures counted in the denominator and bootstrap intervals for two datasets, but gains are best-of-successful and there is no variance over all runs or significance test.

E.cost.reason: Run budget (10 h, two V100) is stated, but the evolved policies' per-query cost, the evolution cost per gain, and a cost-matched baseline are absent.

rationale: Gödel-agent variant for 7B models with a reflect-abstract-patch loop. Table 1 shows the nearest framework barely runs, but gains are best-of-successful runs labelled on test, 35-45% of runs fail, abstraction is unablated and evolved policies spend more calls. Scoped task-level support.
